sources.outlet: Brookings Institution (Robin Brooks and Ben Harris)
sources.quote: Specifically, this means that the U.S. should designate the 524 tankers sanctioned by the EU and UK, but not yet sanctioned by the U.S.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff. Counts US 216, EU 671, UK 627 sanctioned ships; US count unchanged since January 2025; tracks UK-only vessels. Gap is stated for EU+UK combined (524), not UK alone.

sources.outlet: Brookings Institution (Robin Brooks and Ben Harris)
sources.quote: Our updated count for ships sanctioned by the U.S. is 216 (black line), a number that has been unchanged since the final days of the Biden administration in January 2025.
sources.searcher_note: Same page, second quote: the US stopped adding ships in January 2025, the policy slowdown the lead's caveat mentions. Page also says the UK count stands at 627.

sources.quote: To achieve comprehensive coverage across these jurisdictions, the U.S. would need to sanction an additional 518 tankers currently sanctioned by the EU and UK.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff. Says the UK now sanctions 621 ships vs 17 in July 2024 (so nearly all UK listings are 2024-26); US hasn't sanctioned any Russian shadow fleet vessels since Biden.

sources.quote: Only 43 vessels are sanctioned jointly by the US, UK and EU, a number that should be far higher.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest found: US 169, EU 235, UK 174 shadow fleet ships; small overlap between lists. Early version of the same UK/EU vs US gap tracking.

sources.quote: However, President Donald Trump has not imposed new sanctions on Russia in response to its ongoing war in Ukraine.
sources.searcher_note: UK adds 40 shadow fleet vessels (133 total tankers) while the US adds none; early trade-press note of the divergence, no count of the gap.

notes: Brookings (Aug and Sep 2026) tracks the same UK/EU-vs-US sanctioned-ship gap with counts: UK 621-627, US 216, EU+UK-not-US 518-524. No source found that states a UK-only-vs-OFAC gap of 358 or 58%, or that 309 were designated in 2024-25 (Brookings Aug 2026 says UK had 17 ships as of July 2024). Lloyd's List (2025-05-20, paywalled) notes European sanctions in 'stark contrast' to absent US sanctions but was not recorded because only the teaser was reachable. Search snippets suggested a Robin Brooks post saying the US should designate 524 tankers; that figure is on the Brookings Sept 2026 page.
